sheets.title: After the Mauryas: Shungas to Kushanas (185 BCE – 230 CE)
sheets.intro: Shungas, Kanvas, Kharavela, Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians, Kushanas.

rows.v: Shungas (185 – 73 BCE) → Kanvas (73 – 28 BCE)
Chedis (Mahameghavahana) – Kharavela
Satavahanas
Indo-Greeks → Shakas → Parthians → Kushanas ("GSPK")
Foreigners absorbed; Manusmriti calls Shakas, Parthians "fallen Kshatriyas"

keys.name: Pushyamitra Shunga

rows.v: 185 – 149 BCE; Brahmin (Bharadvaja gotra, trad.); Mauryan Senapati
Killed Brihadratha at an army parade (Harshacharita)
Pataliputra, Vidisha; up to the Narmada
Kept "Senapati" (Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva)
Two Ashvamedhas; priest Patanjali (Mahabhashya, Yoga Sutras)
Held off Indo-Greeks (Patanjali – "Yavana besieged Saketa, Madhyamika"; Gargi Samhita – Yavanas reached Pataliputra); Kharavela raids
Divyavadana says he persecuted Buddhists – doubted; Bharhut railings, Sanchi enlarged in his age

traps: Patanjali = Shunga age; Panini much earlier (UPSC 2020 marked "Panini – Pushyamitra" wrong)

rows.v: 149 – 141 BCE; viceroy at Vidisha; war with Yajnasena of Vidarbha; hero of Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram
Beat the Yavanas on the Sindhu (Malavikagnimitram)
Heliodorus pillar at Besnagar (Vidisha), c. 113 BCE
Last; killed by minister Vasudeva Kanva (Harshacharita), 73 BCE
10 kings, about 112 years
Gateway inscription "Suganam raje" (in the reign of the Shungas)

keys.name: Kanvas

rows.v: 73 – 28 BCE; Brahmins (Kanvayanas)
Vasudeva (founder), Bhumimitra (coins in Panchala), Narayana, Susharman (last)
4 kings, about 45 years
Satavahanas ("Andhrabhrityas" in Puranas)

traps: Vasudeva Kanva (king) ≠ Vasudeva Krishna (god of the Heliodorus pillar)

rows.v: Chedi / Mahameghavahana; founder Abhichandra; capital Kalinganagari (Suktimati)
1st century BCE
Maharaja, Kalingadhipati, Bhikshuraja
Udayagiri, Bhubaneswar; Prakrit in Brahmi; year-by-year for 13 years; first to name "Bharatavarsha"
Army west "disregarding Satakarni"; beat Magadha (Brihaspatimitra) – brought back Kalinga Jina taken by Nandaraja; broke a Tamil confederacy; Pandya tribute; a Yavana king fled to Mathura
Extended Nandaraja's canal; Jain council on Kumari hill; caves at Udayagiri – Khandagiri (Ranigumpha – 2 storeys)
Kudepasiri (Manchapuri cave inscription)
Beaten 305 BCE; ceded 4 provinces; Megasthenes sent
Friend of Antiochus I
RE XIII – 5 Greek kings (APAMA): Antiochus II, Ptolemy II, Antigonus Gonatas, Magas, Alexander of Epirus
Diodotus broke away from the Seleucids c. 250 BCE
Yavana / Yona from "Ionian"
Ivory, pearls, indigo, spikenard, malabathrum; Yavana ships at Muziris (Sangam poems)
After 250 BCE; Antiochus III took Kabul
Bactria and Parthia left the Seleucids
Great Wall pushed nomads → Scythians pressed Bactria → Bactrian Greeks moved into India
Mauryan frontier weak after 185 BCE

keys.name: Demetrius

rows.v: Son of Euthydemus (Greco-Bactrian); invaded Afghanistan, Punjab c. 180 BCE
First known Indo-Greek king in India; clashed with Pushyamitra; bilingual square coins
Bactria – controlled Gandhara – West trade routes

traps: Demetrius I was son of Euthydemus, not of Seleucus

rows.v: c. 165/145 – 130 BCE; title Soter (saviour)
Sakala (Sialkot)
Kabul valley to western UP; raids to Mathura, Pataliputra (not held)
Buddhist under Nagasena – Milindapanho (Pali)
Widest spread of any Indo-Greek; Greek gods with Buddhist wheel, lotus
Heliodorus, son of Dion, Greek of Taxila; a Bhagavata
King Antialcidas
Bhagabhadra (Shunga) at Vidisha
Garuda-dhvaja to Vasudeva (Vishnu) at Besnagar – early Vaishnava record
c. 113 BCE

keys.name: Indo-Greek legacy

rows.v: First gold coins in India; first true portrait coins; bilingual Greek + Kharosthi; Athena, Apollo, Zeus with Indian symbols
Hellenistic fusion → Gandhara school; cities Sakala, Ai-Khanoum, Taxila (Sirkap)
Hora (hour, astrology); kendra; Yavanika (stage curtain); Yavanajataka
Shrank after Menander (130 BCE); Shakas (pushed by Yuezhi); last king Strato II (c. 10 CE); Hermaius's fall opened the NW

traps: First gold coins = Indo-Greeks; much gold = Kushanas; finest gold = Guptas

rows.v: Pushed by the Yuezhi and Chinese wars
Afghanistan (Vonones, Spalirises); Punjab – Taxila (Maues / Moga); Mathura (Azilises; satraps Rajuvula, Sodasa – Mathura Lion Capital); western India – Ujjain; upper Deccan
Mahasenapati; Satrap / Kshatrapa (Persian system); Mahakshatrapa
Married into Indian houses; Shiva, Vishnu, Buddhism; saddles, reins; coat, trousers, boots
Bhumaka, Nahapana
Nasik – Pune, Gujarat coast
Nahapana beaten by Gautamiputra Satakarni; his coins restruck (Jogalthembi hoard)

keys.name: Rudradaman I

rows.v: Kardamaka Shakas of Ujjain; founder Chashtana (Ptolemy's "Tiastenes of Ozene")
Gujarat, Sindh, Kutch, Kathiawar, Konkan, Malwa
Beat them twice; spared – daughter married Vasishthiputra Satakarni
150 CE (Saka year 72); first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit (Brahmi)
Repaired Sudarshana from own treasury – no forced labour (vishti) or new tax; governor Suvishakha (a Pahlava)
Western Kshatrapa silver coins – first Indian coins with dates (Saka era)
Rudrasimha III beaten by Chandragupta II (c. 409 CE)

traps: Nahapana lost to Gautamiputra; Rudradaman beat the Satavahanas later

rows.v: c. 250 BCE – 14 Major Rock Edicts (Prakrit)
150 CE – Sanskrit; lake repair
c. 455 CE – lake dam repaired again (Parnadatta, Chakrapalita)
Pushyagupta (Chandragupta) built; Tushaspha (Ashoka) channels; Suvishakha (Rudradaman) repaired

keys.name: Vikram and Saka eras

rows.v: 58/57 BCE; legend of Vikramaditya of Ujjain beating the Shakas; earlier Krita, Malava era
78 CE; credited to Kanishka (debated); used by Western Kshatrapas
Saka, adopted 22 March 1957 (1 Chaitra 1879); first month Chaitra; Saka year = CE − 78
135 years
319 – 320 CE (third era)

traps: Chandragupta II "Vikramaditya, Shakari" beat the Shakas c. 409 CE – a different Vikramaditya

keys.name: Parthians (Pahlavas)

rows.v: Iran; with Shakas ("Shaka-Pahlavas")
c. 19 – 46 CE; founded the Indo-Parthian kingdom at Taxila; Takht-i-Bahi inscription (45 CE, near Mardan – UNESCO monastery)
Acts of Thomas – at the court of "Gudnaphar"; martyred at Mylapore (Chennai)
Abdagases lost to the Kushanas

traps: Takht-i-Bahi is near Mardan, not Taxila

rows.v: Yuezhi (Yue-chi) of China's frontier; Kushana branch moved into Gandhara, Kabul
c. 15 – 64 CE; united the tribes; coins mostly copper (source says gold)
Soter Megas (Rabatak)
c. 64 – 78 CE; to Mathura; plenty of gold coins; Shiva and Nandi on coins
Purushapura (Peshawar), Mathura
Central Asia to the Ganga; Khorasan to Varanasi; coins at Mathura, Sravasti, Kausambi, Sarnath
Maharaja, Rajatiraja, Devaputra (son of god), Kaisara (Caesar)
Mahayana patron; 4th council at Kundalavana, Kashmir (Vasumitra, Ashvaghosha; Mahavibhasha in Sanskrit)
Ashvaghosha (Buddhacharita), Vasumitra, Nagarjuna, Parshva, Charaka (Charaka Samhita), Mathara
Kanishka stupa at Shah-ji-ki-Dheri, Peshawar (Agesilaus); relic casket
Headless, at Mat near Mathura – long coat, boots
Buddha with "BODDO"; Greek, Iranian, Indian gods
Rabatak inscription (1993, Bactrian in Greek script); Rajatarangini (Kalhana)
78 CE
Satrapies under Mahakshatrapas; Dandanayaka, Mahadandanayaka; Gramika, Padrapala; dual rule (father – son)
Silk Route control; Indo-Roman trade
Gold (trade; Shiva, Buddha, Zeus), silver, copper; Roman weight standard; first large-scale gold coinage
Mahayana, Shaiva, Vaishnava – tolerance
Gandhara (grey schist, Greek look), Mathura (red sandstone, Indian) – first human Buddha images
Charaka (Ayurveda), Nagarjuna (Madhyamika), Vatsyayana (Kamasutra, by tradition)
Vasudeva I (Shiva worshipper), early 3rd c.
Sasanians (Persia) in Central Asia; Chinese general Pan Chao beat them in Central Asia
Broke into small kingdoms → Guptas rose
Satrap system, Gandhara and Mathura art, Mahayana spread to China
Ashoka built; Shungas enlarged; toranas with Jatakas (carvers of Vidisha); on Dakshinapatha
Satna; found by Cunningham; red stone rails; Mayadevi's dream, Ruru Jataka
White limestone; Buddha's life (Satavahanas)
Udayagiri – Khandagiri (Kharavela); early Ajanta (Hinayana)
Mathura (red sandstone), Gandhara (grey schist), Amaravati (white)
Brahmanism back; rigid varna; Manusmriti limits women; foreigners as mixed castes
Guilds; Mathura's shataka cloth; Uttarapatha, Dakshinapatha; monsoon sea trade to Rome
